items.title: New mayor in Mississauga, but familiar faces return to city council
items.summary: Mississauga voters let it be known on Monday they want change at the top, but they’re just fine with their city councillors. While Alvin Tedjo soundly defeated incumbent Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie in a mayoral victory that several months ago not many political watchers would’ve predicted, all incumbent Mississauga councillors who ran for reelection were successful. The only new faces who’ll be on city council when it convenes for its next term in mid-November are those who’ll occupy the wards 2 and 7 seats vacated by Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, respectively. Damerla, with 11,500 votes, finished in fourth place in the mayoral race, well back of Tedjo (74,479 votes), Parrish (51,853 votes) and Crombie (43,191 votes). m. Monday. items.title: Who is Alvin Tedjo? 4 things to know about the winner of Mississauga’s mayoral race
items.summary: He was a first-term councillor and a long-shot candidate. From high school student council to an unlikely win, here’s what to know about Alvin Tedjo. Alvin Tedjo, a first-term councillor, has been elected mayor of Mississauga. He grew up with a view of City Hall outside his house. Now, he will be Mississauga’s mayor. Alvin Tedjo, a first-term councillor and former provincial political staffer, staged an unlikely campaign against two titans of Mississauga politics — former mayor Bonnie Crombie and incumbent Carolyn Parrish — to ride to victory on Monday. Here are four things to know about Tedjo. Tedjo’s Chinese-Indonesian parents settled in Mississauga when he was four and he grew up downtown, where he could see City Hall from outside his house. “I saw a lot of the challenges and hardships that come with that immigrant experience,” he said on a 2025 podcast. “If you see something wrong, do something about it,” he said his parents taught him. He was student council president in high school and served on the mayor’s youth advisory committee. He met then-mayor Hazel McCallion in the mid-1990s, when he won an award for being Young Citizen of the Year. “Get into politics, young man,” she told him, he said.

Alvin Tedjo may have started the Mississauga mayoral election as an underdog, but he has managed to beat out former mayor Bonnie Crombie and incumbent Carolyn Parrish to take over the city’s top job, CityNews projects. He won handidly, leading Parrish in second by over 20,000 votes, despite early polls showing a tight race leading up to election. “Our optimism, our hope, our vision for what this city could be, our positivity and our unstoppable effort to reach every single resident in the city of Mississauga, to put forward practical solutions that would make a difference in their lives and to earn their trust, all of that hard work has led us to this moment,” said Tedjo in his victory speech.

items.title: Rookie Councillor's Six-Month Climb From Fourth Place Ends in Mississauga's Top Job
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Alvin Tedjo, a first-term city councillor, has won Mississauga's mayoral race after his campaign started in a distant fourth place six months ago. According to the newspaper, the 43-year-old overtook incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor, former mayor and Ontario Liberal leader Bonnie Crombie, who had held a narrow lead in polling heading into election day. The Star reports that with 89 per cent of polls reporting on election night, Tedjo led by more than 18,000 votes. At his victory party, Tedjo told cheering supporters that Mississauga had voted for change, and said that when his team started out, people had told them they could not win. According to the outlet, Crombie called Tedjo to congratulate him and, standing on stage with her three children, said his energy and enthusiasm had inspired people to believe they could help shape the city's future.

items.title: What residents should know as they vote on election day in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga residents are casting their ballots today and this evening following months of campaigning by candidates running for mayor, city council and school board trustee positions. Headlining the 2026 municipal election in Mississauga is a hotly contested mayoral race featuring four main candidates — including the current mayor and her predecessor — among a larger field of 14 hopefuls vying for the city’s top elected office. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie, who traded pointed attacks during the campaign’s high-stakes debates, are attempting to fend off challenges from city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla. Campaign watchers in Mississauga — and several polls — note more recently Tedjo appears to have garnered additional support that has perhaps vaulted him into a close three-way race as election night arrives. Record numbers turned out for advance voting Municipal election voters who didn’t cast ballots earlier this month during record-setting advance polling in Mississauga are doing so today and tonight. m. across the city. The victorious candidates will serve in their positions for the next term of office, which runs from 2026-2030.
